themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% increase (z-score: 7.78)—suggesting rapid neighborhood tensions over sidewalk dining expansion or enforcement gaps in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 7.78)
Spike is freshest signal in dataset—emerged within last 7 days
Suggests acute neighborhood friction over either new dining sheds, inadequate spacing, or enforcement inconsistency
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents and business owners on DeKalb Avenue or Myrtle Avenue to understand what triggered sudden complaints
Investigate whether DOE&P recently issued new outdoor dining permits or modified enforcement approach in the district

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK compared to a 1.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—a 433% surge (z-score: 4.63)—potentially signaling storm damage, disease outbreak, or sudden neighborhood awareness of tree health crisis in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score: 4.63)
Emerged this week alongside SPIT (Special Projects Inspection Team) spike, suggesting coordinated tree inspection activity
Could reflect post-storm damage assessment, seasonal disease (e.g., spotted lanternfly, emerald ash borer), or deferred Parks maintenance
reporting_angles: Check NYC Parks tree survey data and maintenance records for Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights to identify problem corridors
Interview Parks Department on recent tree health assessments and whether drought, pests, or storm damage is driving spike

themes_detail.label: NYPD Investigations & Discipline Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about NYPD Investigations and Discipline (IAD) surged to 6 LAST WEEK versus 0.2 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 13.28)—following the April 16 Hell Gate/Brooklyn Eagle reporting of detectives punching wrong man during a Boerum Hill drug bust, suggesting community anger over police conduct in the district.
evidence: 6 IAD complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 13.28)
Timing aligns with April 16 Brooklyn Eagle article on NYPD detectives punching wrong man in Boerum Hill drug bust—likely complaints were filed in response
Highest statistical z-score (13.28) in entire dataset indicates most severe anomaly
reporting_angles: Follow up on Boerum Hill drug bust incident: interview victim, obtain complaint/IA filing details, and track case status
Analyze NYPD complaint patterns in CD 302 over past 12 months—are there other use-of-force incidents or pattern complaints?

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints exploded to 16 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.9 per week over 8 weeks—a 1729% spike (z-score: 14.36)—indicating either aggressive new enforcement campaign or community frustration with enforcement tactics in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 16 real-time enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1729% spike, z-score: 14.36)
Second-highest z-score in dataset, indicating statistically extreme anomaly
May reflect new police or DOE&P enforcement initiative, or community reporting spike tied to visible enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Check with NYPD and DOE&P on any new enforcement blitz, saturation deployment, or policy change announced 1–2 weeks ago
Interview residents and community leaders on what enforcement activity they witnessed and whether it was perceived as fair or aggressive

themes_detail.label: Electrical Hazards Spike
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 6 LAST WEEK versus 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 586% increase (z-score: 5.53)—possibly indicating storm damage, aging infrastructure deterioration, or unsafe street vendor equipment in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% spike, z-score: 5.53)
Converges with outdoor dining spike THIS WEEK—may reflect hazardous wiring on new/existing dining sheds or street vendor equipment
Could also indicate post-weather electrical damage to street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details to map which streets/blocks reported electrical hazards and investigate specific hazard types
Cross-reference with Con Edison incident reports and outage data for the district during the past 2 weeks
